description: email.rs filter_properties (line 1232) and apply_body_properties (line 1199) iterate the source map with .iter() and call .clone() on every surviving key and value. Because these functions consume their input by reference (part: &Value, obj: &Value), a move is impossible — the clone is forced. However the call sites in apply_body_value_args own the values in the list (parts.iter_mut()), so the idiomatic design would be to take the body part by value (part: Value) and use into_iter() to move surviving entries without allocating. For email responses that include large HTML bodies this is a measurable allocation saving (every surviving key string and every value is deep-cloned). The apply_body_properties_recursive function already takes &mut Value, making the transition straightforward. The same pattern applies to filter_properties called from handle_email_get.
title: filter_properties and apply_body_properties clone every key and value — avoids move
